alex k: heads up — seeing ~15% tail latency regression on paged-attn after allocator refactor (slab->dynamic-slab). P50 34ms -> 39ms, P99 120ms -> 140ms on T4 (seq=1024, batch=8).

maria r: hmm, when did this land?

alex k: merged yesterday afternoon. ran bench: `./bench/paged_attn --model=gpt2 --seq=1024 --bsz=8 --iters=500`

sam t: any flamegraphs?

perf-bot: flamegraph: http://perf.internal/fg/1783456789 (shows memcpy hotspots)

alex k: profiler shows memcpy and GPU small-buffer churn up the stack. KV block allocations are creating many small GPU buffers (~128B-4KB) which cause driver overhead and scheduling stalls.

maria r: can we use a pre-allocated pool with chunking? also track fragmentation metric (free_bytes / total_bytes). what fragmentation numbers do we see?

alex k: fragmentation ~22% after 10k requests in the bench. Block table entry count keeps growing, a lot of slots are reserved but unused.

jin: my earlier paged-attn design used per-size-class free-lists + lightweight headers. we simplified to a single global freelist to reduce bookkeeping, but that likely causes size-class fragmentation.

sam t: propose switching to segregated free lists (power-of-two classes) + a deferred compaction/coalesce pass every N allocations. pseudocode:
```
if size <= 4KB: cls = round_up_pow2(size)
alloc = freelist[cls].pop() // O(1)
if freelist[cls] empty: split larger slab and push into smaller freelists
periodic_compact(): scan blocktable, coalesce adjacent free blocks, refill freelists
```
This should reduce small-buffer churn and driver calls.

alex k: ran a quick patch replacing global freelist with segregated freelists — median improved slightly, p99 dropped to 126ms (from 140ms). still chasing a ~4% residual.

maria r: nice. also revisit kernel selection heuristic. for some configs fused-attn + FlashA-v2 outperforms paged-attn; for others paged-attn has better memory profile. we need adaptive selection.

jin: current selector: `if seq * batch < 8192 then fused else paged`. bench sweep shows a boundary closer to 12k on T4 with FlashA-v2 and our quant profiles.

alex k: matrix I ran (seq=1024,batch=8): FlashA-v2 fused median=31ms, paged median=37ms but paged uses ~1.8x less GPU memory. For batch=1 paged wins by a bigger margin.

sam t: suggestion: incorporate `kv_density` into the heuristic where `kv_density = avg_kv_blocks_per_seq / seq_len`. high kv_density favors paged to avoid huge memory spikes. Also weight by per-request latency SLO.

maria r: add a cheap runtime probe: sample the last N requests to compute kv_density and pick kernel per-route. also add fallback policy if chosen kernel OOMs or p99 exceeds threshold.

alex k: added metrics proposal: emit `kv.alloc.size_class`, `kv.fragmentation_pct`, `paged_attn.kernel_choice`, `paged_attn.kv_density` to our console and Prom. can use these for CI gating.

perf-bot: created ticket PERF-2912: bench logs + flamegraph attached -> http://perf.internal/fg/1783456789

jin: I'll open a PR with freelist+deferred-compact and a small microbench that compares before/after on T4 and p3.2xlarge. Will include the fragmentation counter and unit tests for freelist invariants.

sam t: also add a CI microbench that runs in the merge pipeline (short run, seq=512, bsz=2) and fails if p99 regresses >5% vs baseline binary.

maria r: sounds good. assign to @jin, cc @sam, I'll review. please include a one-off flamegraph in the PR description.

alex k: thanks. after PR lands I'll run a longer night run to verify no regressions on larger models and do a canary rollout to Dedicated pools.

jin: will do. expected PR by EOD.

sam t: FYI we should also tweak the blocktable eviction heuristic: prefer evicting large contiguous free ranges to reduce fragmentation instead of LRU single-slot evictions.

maria r: agreed. add to the PR as an optional strategy behind a feature flag so we can A/B it.

alex k: great. I'll keep monitoring metrics and post updates here. :thumbsup:
